sentences.text: The petitioner, for espousing the cause mentioned in the petition, is seeking appropriate directions against the respondents to initiate proceedings under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') against the manufacturer of AAVA Natural Mineral Water, contending, inter alia, that the advertisement is misleading and there is misbranding of the product and the prayer is made that such would be in the larger public interest.
3. In response to the notice issued by this Court, affidavits-in-reply have been filed by the respondents.

4. We have heard Mr.Rao, learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, Mr.Devnani, learned AGP for respondents No.1 and 2, Mr.Kavina, learned Sr. Counsel appearing for respondent No.6,
Mr.Bhagyodaya Mishra, learned Counsel for respondent No.5, Mr.Vaishnav, learned Counsel appearing for respondent No.3, and Ms.Contractor, HC-NIC Page 2 of 6 Created On Thu Dec 10 00:27:35 IST 2015 learned Counsel appearing for Ms.Raval for respondent No.4 Corporation.
5.

Upon hearing the learned Counsel for both the sides, it appears to us that the contention of the petitioner is that the product is misbranded and it is not natural mineral water, which is being sold by respondent No.6, whereas, as per respondent No.6, there is no misbranding of the product and the product, which is being sold, is natural mineral water.

6. As per the petitioner, the samples were taken, but it did not meet with the standards, whereas, as per respondent No.6 as well as Food Analyst, who is represented by the AGP and respondent No.5 - Bureau of Indian Standards, it meets with the requirements.

There are allegations and counter- allegations, but considering the facts and circumstances, we find that if the testing of the water,
which is being marketed and sold by respondent No.6, is undertaken by competent authority under Section 47 of the Act, such would not cause any prejudice, since even otherwise also, as per the mechanism of the Act, Food Analyst or the competent authority under the Act HC-NIC Page 3 of 6 Created On Thu Dec 10 00:27:35 IST 2015 has power to take the samples and undertake the testing.
7. The essential attempt on the part of the petitioner was to see that the authority is activated for appropriate action in accordance with law.

8. When it was put to the learned AGP, appearing for the competent authority, including respondent No.2 for the fresh samples to be taken and undertaking the exercise of testing of such samples as per the requirements of Section 47 of the Act and for consideration of the matter under Section 46 of the Act, the learned AGP has stated that the authority, Food Analyst will have no objection for such purpose.

9. Even Mr.Kavina, learned Sr. Counsel for respondent No.6, has not opposed the same, contending that the product, which is being marketed by them, is meeting with the requirements and there could not be any objection for undertaking the test.

sentences.text: In view of the above, we find that the Food Analyst of concerning area shall take the samples of the product of respondent No.6, shall examine HC-NIC Page 4 of 6 Created On Thu Dec 10 00:27:35 IST 2015 the correct branding and purity of the product, by following the procedure as per the requirements of Section 47 of the Act.

The samples shall be tested with appropriate Laboratory and if it is found that the samples are meeting with the requisite standards and there is no misbranding,
the same shall be communicated to the petitioner.
In the event it is found that the samples are not meeting with the standards and there is no misbranding, the Food Analyst shall take appropriate action in accordance with law.

11. It is also clarified that if the samples of the product of respondent No.6 are found to be meeting with the standards and there is no misbranding, even as per the decision taken by Food Analyst and the same is communicated to the petitioner and thereafter if the petitioner is aggrieved by such decision, he may resort to appropriate proceedings under Sub-section (4) of Section 46 of the Act before the designated authority.
12.

In our view, the aforesaid observations and directions shall take care of the larger public HC-NIC Page 5 of 6 Created On Thu Dec 10 00:27:35 IST 2015 interest and no further order deserves to be passed.

13. We may record that Mr.Kavina, learned Sr. Counsel appearing for respondent No.6 had made submissions that the conduct of the petitioner is deplorable and no writ may be entrusted to him,
but we have not gone into such allegations or counter-allegations, in order to see that if the statutory authority is activated for testing of the sample, which is the product of drinking water, no prejudice would be caused to either side.
Hence, we do not find it appropriate to make any further observations in this regard.
14. The petition is disposed of accordingly.
No order as to costs.
(JAYANT PATEL, ACJ.) (VIPUL M. PANCHOLI, J.) vinod
